DISTRIBUTION. — Blackites aff. gladius is only known from three records, one in Belgium, one in the Paris Basin and one in the Aquitaine Basin. It rarely co-occurs with Blackites inflatus in the Isnes quarry in SW Belgium, where its presence seems to be restricted to the top of the Brussel Sand Formation. A few specimens have been identified in the Donzacq Marl (upper NP 14) at Saint-Geoursd’Auribat (Aquitaine Basin) (Lin et al. 2017) and in the upper part of the ‘ Glauconie Grossière s. s. ’ at Margival (Paris Basin, sample 3 in Steurbaut 1988), where it also co-occurs with B. inflatus. B. aff. gladius seems to indicate late Biochron NP 14, also known as Biochon NP 14 b (sensu Berggren et al. 1995). It has not been recorded at the Mont-des-Récollets because of major erosion of the top of the Brussel Sand Formation in N France.
